sections.heading: MOD reverse complete
items: The DMC3 HD MOD reverse is complete for the canonical project scope: the serialized format, runtime-facing model contract and source-preservation boundaries all have terminal evidence states.

Reverse complete does not mean every byte received a speculative artistic name. PRESERVED_UNDECODED, RESERVED_OBSERVED_ZERO and REJECTED are valid terminal outcomes where stronger semantics are not evidenced.
The public MOD section therefore separates a completed reverse/reader contract from the still-bounded writer, archive reintegration and original-game acceptance programs.

sections.heading: Canonical MOD map
items: The recovered contract covers the 0x40 document header, 0x40 object records, 0x50 mesh records, position/normal/fixed-point UV streams, blend indices, packed skin weights and topology control.

Hierarchy/order, default-joint behavior, local/world transforms, inverse-rest/current-world skin palette construction, post-load relocation and generated topology workspace behavior are part of the canonical MOD runtime map.

Texture-slot selection, GS CLAMP state, the external texture-companion/runtime-descriptor relationship, object runtime projection and the MOD-side MOT/CMotion boundary are also recovered without collapsing neighboring resource families into MOD.

sections.heading: Terminal preservation outcomes
items: Header +0x14 is a runtime-carried u32 and the old universal decimal family/model/sub-index interpretation is rejected for MOD.
BLENDINDICES.x remains a serialized ABI lane while the audited compiled shader path consumes Y/Z/W; source flag 0x00200000 is runtime-carried/restored without an invented artistic label.

Mesh +0x38 is family-sensitive and inactive on the audited MOD path while its EFM homologue is live; mesh +0x0C/+0x4C and transform +0x1C retain explicit preservation contracts instead of being mislabeled as padding.

sections.heading: Writer and reintegration are separate gates
items: Preserve-Layout Writer Gate 1 supports bounded fixed-size edits over an immutable source image, and the provenance-bound retail no-op corpus passes 38/38 files across 882,736 source bytes with exact byte parity and canonical reopen.

One controlled retail bounding-radius edit changes exactly three authorized bytes, and the authored child has a provenance-bound real retail PNST reintegration receipt plus a synthetic MOD-to-NBZ overlay reopen gate.

Typed-IR-only reflow, transform/skin/material/texture-companion authoring, provenance-bound retail NBZ acceptance and original dmc3.exe acceptance remain open authoring/integration work; they do not reopen the MOD reverse.

lessons.title: 01 — What is MOD?
lessons.description: Start with the completed DMC3 HD MOD reverse, the resource's role and the separation between reverse completeness and writer/original-game acceptance.

lessons.title: 02 — Document, objects and meshes
lessons.description: Walk through the canonical document/object/mesh contract, header boundaries, object state and preservation-aware mesh fields.

lessons.title: 03 — Skeleton, hierarchy and transforms
lessons.description: Study parent/order topology, local/world transforms, inverse-rest relationships and the terminal preservation boundary for transform +0x1C.

lessons.title: 04 — Skinning, topology and shader inputs
lessons.description: Follow packed influences and topology generation through the shader ABI, including BLENDINDICES Y/Z/W consumption and the preserved X lane.

lessons.title: 05 — Textures and materials
lessons.description: Relate texture slots and companions to runtime material state and EXE-confirmed GS-facing selectors without inventing artistic categories.

lessons.title: 06 — Animation and motion groups
lessons.description: Understand the recovered motion-group and MOD-side animation-binding boundary while keeping MOT/CMotion as its own authority.

lessons.title: 07 — Related formats
lessons.description: Compare MOD with SCM, SHW, EFM, MOT, SO and texture companions so neighboring systems are not mistaken for unfinished MOD reverse.

lessons.title: 08 — Evidence and terminal unknowns
lessons.description: Learn why preservation-only and rejected outcomes are valid terminal reverse states rather than invitations to invent semantics.

lessons.title: 09 — Reverse workflow
lessons.description: Review the evidence workflow that closed MOD: raw bytes, executable evidence, corpus validation, hypothesis rejection, terminal classification and promotion.

lessons.title: 10 — Exercises and debugging
lessons.description: Practice diagnosing offsets, counts, hierarchy relationships, transform mistakes and skin/topology problems using the completed canonical contract.

lessons.title: MOD glossary
lessons.description: Reference current MOD terminology, terminal evidence classes, runtime metadata, GS state selectors and skinning ABI.

lessons.title: MOD reference map
lessons.description: Jump from the completed MOD learning surface to canonical code, tests, research notes and evidence receipts.
